rename.from: [ML] Improve datafeed performance by skipping time periods without data
rename.to: [ML] Slow performance for datafeeds with aggs when there are long periods without data

issue.title: [ML] Skip time to next interval with data for datafeeds with aggs

labels.name: Team:ML
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
This commit improves performance of datafeeds using aggs and chunking.
In particular, it alignes this case with what happens for scrolling datafeeds.
The `ChunkedDataExtractor` already has an optimization in place where if a
search returns no data, it reconfigures itself by looking at the next time
interval where data exists. It then advances time accordingly or completes
if no data could be found.

The reason the optimization does not work for datafeeds with aggs is that
datafeeds with aggs do not return an empty `Optional` when `next()` is called
like the `ChunkedDataExtractor` expects. Instead, they do return an `InputStream`
that contains zero bytes. This commit fixes this issue.

Closes #82406
